https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/24/oros.text: Menü Kereső Oroszország is részt vesz a decemberi G20-csúcson Külföld Pupli Anna Sára Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Oroszország biztosan részt vesz a decemberi G20-csúcson, amit Miamiban rendeznek meg, jelentette be csütörtökön Dmitrij Peszkov, az orosz elnök sajtótitkára a TASZSZ orosz állami hírügynökség szerint. Arról viszont, hogy Vlagyimir Putyin elfogadja-e Marco Rubio amerikai külügyminiszter meghívását , Peszkov szerint még nem döntöttek. „A kérdést alaposan át fogjuk vizsgálni, és csak ezután születik meg a megfelelő döntés” – jegyezte meg a Kreml szóvivője. „Mindenesetre Oroszország szándékában áll továbbra is részt venni a G20 munkájában és az ennek keretében megrendezett valamennyi fórumon.” Rubio szerdán azt mondta, a Trump-kormány reméli, hogy Putyin elfogadja a meghívást, ami a külügyminiszter szerint akár az alapját is képezheti egy szélesebb körű megállapodásnak. Szerinte a meghívással azért sincs gond, mert a nemzetközi kapcsolatokban az egymással egyet nem értő feleknek is szükséges találkozni és tárgyalni, különben lehetetlen lenne megoldani ezeket a vitákat. Peszkov egyébként szintén szerdán beszélt arról egy sajtótájékoztatón , hogy Putyin kész találkozni Trumppal, de akkor még nem volt szó a G20-as csúcsról. Stasys Eidrigevičius And Everywhere I See a Face Graphotography October 30, 2026–February 14, 2027 Add to Calendar Exhibition opening: October 30, 6pm, featuring the performance The Birth of a Painting by artist Stasys Eidrigevičius Add to Calendar Stasys Museum Respublikos st. 40 Panevezys LT-35173 Lithuania Hours: Tuesday –Saturday 11am–7pm Sunday 11am–5pm info@stasysmuseum.com stasysmuseum.com Facebook / Instagram Stasys Eidrigevičius and the faces that surround him The photographs in which artist Stasys Eidrigevičius captured his parents and loved ones during childhood awaken memories, evoke a sense of tradition, and inspire respect. His paintings, by contrast, often provoke laughter, creating a witty and at times subtly grotesque atmosphere. These seemingly contradictory modes of perception converge in the artistic genre Eidrigevičius has been developing in recent years: graphotography . Bringing together the traditionally distinct disciplines of photography and drawing within the digital realm, graphotography may be understood as a form of photographic image transformed through digital intervention. In Eidrigevičius’s work, it serves as yet another means of expressing a unique creative vision of the world around him. Eidrigevičius is constantly sketching. Today, his sketchbook has been replaced by a smartphone and tablet, through which he playfully and ironically reprogrammes the views that surround him. “I see a face everywhere,” the artist says. He follows paths shaped by both nature and humans, returns in memory to the countryside, plays with fragments of recollection, and dives deep into reflections on the relationship between past and present, the persistence and transformation of values, creative processes, and the junctions between generations. He mourns and laughs. Symbolically, such contrasting emotions emerge through a combination of traditional artistic methods and contemporary technologies. Photographs of architectural motifs that evoke historical memory, elements of the natural and urban landscape, and details of everyday life are later complemented by digital drawings. Within these spaces, Eidrigevičius inserts pairs of small eyes that have become a signature feature of his artistic language, while digitally drawn portrait or profile lines create new images. Japanese audiences were the first to recognise Eidrigevičius’s graphotographic works. More than a decade ago, the artist began collaborating with the renowned Japanese writer and art historian Motoko Nakagawa. Their partnership focused on books in which Nakagawa wrote the texts and Eidrigevičius created colourful, evocative, and highly original illustrations. In 2022, the artist began digitally drawing over photographs and sending the resulting images to Nakagawa. Their usual working method was reversed: the visual narrative emerged first, followed by texts written in response to the images. This collaboration has since resulted in five books published in Japanese. In their most recent publication, the authors explore the relationship between Eidrigevičius’s masks and the realities of the pandemic. Eidrigevičius’s graphotography brings together personal and collective experiences, creating a visual dialogue between tradition and innovation. Presented in Lithuania for the first time, these digitally transformed images – accompanied by essays inspired by real people, objects, and events – invite viewers to look more closely at the world around them, to reflect on it, and to embrace the act of creation. https://www.oann.com/newsroom/freedom-of.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (C), alongside Poland’s Foreign Minister Radosaw Sikorski (L) and Burundi’s Foreign Minister Édouard Bizimana (R), speaks as he chairs the first plenary session during the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, Georgia on October 30, 2026. (Photo by Erik S. Lesser / AFP via Getty Images) OAN Staff Addie Davis 10:02 AM – Sunday, November 1, 2026 The G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting wrapped up in Atlanta, Georgia, over the weekend, with United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating that freedom of navigation was a focal point for the assembly. Rubio specifically condemned the attacks on commercial shipping by Iran as well as hostilities from the Iranian-backed terrorist group, the Houthis. Since the advent of the U.S.-Iran conflict at the end of February, disruption to international energy routes have made global shockwaves, especially with the de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz early in the conflict. Though U.S. officials have asserted that the transit of commercial vessels, which U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) reported have brought more than one and a half billion barrels of oil into the global market since summer, continues through the vital waterway with the assistance of American forces, the Iranian threat to shipping has led to volatility in the energy sector. “We now live in a world where the Iranian regime actively and openly targets commercial vessels for attack — not naval vessels; we’re not talking about naval vessels; we’re not talking about submarines,” Rubio stated at a press conference on Saturday . “We are talking about them saying, ‘Here’s a commercial vessel with cargo, oil, natural gas, and we are going to try to sink it.’” “They are openly attacking vessels as a tool of statecraft. That’s the world we live in, and I think Central Command and the United States has done a phenomenal job of protecting this shipping,” the secretary continued. Rubio also referenced the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, where hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have escalated in recent months, and the “hostile coercion” seen in the South China Sea and the Strait of Taiwan. At the closing @G20org Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, I made clear to our partners that secure supply chains are essential for growth. Critical trade routes including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb Strait must remain secure and open to commerce. And we must continue to… pic.twitter.com/8vhPGnG4NO — Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) October 31, 2026 According to a Saturday statement from the chair of the meeting, a position designated to the host country, the ministers specifically discussed the topics of energy security, supply chain resilience and geopolitical tensions, which included the Straits of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb. Rubio noted that under the administration of President Donald Trump, the U.S. has pushed for “the G20 to get back to basics.” “But the core of this meeting and the core of what the president’s vision has been for G20 is to bring the G20, which is primarily an economic forum, back to its core principle and purpose, and that’s what we tried to address in the agenda we outlined today,” the secretary noted on Saturday. The G20 has 19 country participants , as well as two regional governing bodies — the African Union and the European Union — and Rubio recognized that the initial obstacle to reaching consensus was identifying the problems. “But I think the first step is at least some universal acknowledgment that freedom of navigation matters, that critical minerals matter, that supply chains matter, that food security matters, not just to the countries at the table but to countries around the world, and I do think we have that,” he told reporters. However, he explained that agreement on solutions was a different matter for the forum. “Of course, I wouldn’t pretend to you today that we are close to finding universally accepted solutions to these problems, but I do think that among the G20 represented here are countries that are working together to solve some of them, particularly in the realm of supply chains and critical minerals,” he said. On the sidelines of the weekend’s ministerial, Rubio also met with several foreign ministers, including engaging in discussions with the Quad – the U.S., Australia, India and Japan – to address “progress on ongoing Quad initiatives and reaffirm commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific” The State Department noted that October’s meeting was meant to set the stage for the G20 Leaders’ Summit in December, which the U.S. president will host, with world leaders convening in Miami, Florida. In Atlanta, @SecRubio led @G20org countries back to their core mission: Drive economic growth and strengthen economic security. The United States will continue leading these efforts with our partners in December at the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Miami, concluding our G20 presidency… pic.twitter.com/1Zdbx7U7w4 — Department of State (@StateDept) November 1, 2026 CORRECTION – 3:45 PM: ‘Bab al-Mandab’ changed to ‘Bab el-Mandeb’ Stay informed!
